transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess what made me finally decide to come in is that... for the past few weeks, my eating has just been really off. I’ll end up skipping breakfast and lunch without really meaning to. And then I just kind of pick at dinner, even when my wife cooked. I'm noticing my jeans are starting to feel pretty loose, too, so I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
Over these past few weeks when your eating has been off, how has your mood been? Have you been feeling sad, empty, or down most of the time?

Yeah, I have. Most days lately, I just wake up with this... really heavy, flat feeling. It's like the apartment is just too quiet, you know? And usually I'd play some music or something, but lately even picking up my guitar doesn't really lift me out of it. So, yeah, I've definitely been feeling pretty down most of the time.
Have you experienced episodes like this before in your life, where you felt this way for weeks or longer?
No, not really. I mean, I've had days where I felt a little off or tired, but... nothing like this, where it just drags on for weeks and I can't seem to shake it. This is definitely new for me.
When did you first notice these feelings of heaviness and the changes in your eating start? Can you think back to when this all began?

I'd say it's been about three weeks now. This whole... low stretch, I guess, started right after my wife settled into her full-time work schedule. That's when I really noticed the heaviness setting in and my appetite dropping off.
You mentioned these feelings started after your wife settled into her full-time work schedule. Was there something specific about that change that was particularly difficult or stressful for you?

Not exactly stressful, no. It's just... well, since I'm not working right now, she was kind of my main company during the day, or at least she was around a lot more. Now that she's gone all day, it's just me in the apartment. 

I wouldn't say it caused a big conflict or anything like that. It's just... a really noticeable shift. It gets pretty lonely and quiet, I guess, and I just haven't really adjusted to it.

Besides your wife starting her full-time work schedule, has anything else significant or upsetting happened in your life during these past few weeks — like a loss, conflict, health concern, or any other major life change?

No, not really. Um... I can't think of anything else. There haven't been any big arguments or health issues or anything like that. It's really just been her schedule changing. Everything else in my life has been pretty much exactly the same.

Do you feel like your low mood and loss of appetite are a direct result of your wife being gone during the day, or do you think these feelings might have happened anyway even if her schedule hadn't changed?

I don't really know, honestly. I mean... the timing definitely lines up with her going back to work, so it feels connected. But at the same time, I'm not sure if it's just the quietness of the apartment causing all this, or if it would have hit me anyway. It's hard to say for sure.

If your wife were to suddenly go back to working from home or spending more time with you during the day, do you think your mood and appetite would improve and return to normal, or do you feel like these feelings have kind of taken on their own momentum now?

Um... I'm not really sure, to be honest. I'd like to think it would help if she was home more, but... it kind of feels like I'm stuck in this rut now. 

Even if her schedule changed back tomorrow, I don't know if my appetite and mood would just snap back to normal right away. It feels like it's sort of settled in at this point, I guess.

When you think about your mood and appetite problems now, do they feel like they're completely about missing your wife during the day, or do they feel like something deeper — like a depression that just happened to start around that time?

I'm really not sure. Um... it's hard to separate the two, you know? Like, I definitely miss her being around, but... I don't know if I'd call it something deeper, or if it's just a depression that started then. It just feels like I'm really down, and it started when she went back to work. I don't really know how to categorize it beyond that.

When you think about feeling this way over the past three weeks, does it feel like your low mood is something that's happening inside you — like your brain chemistry or something — or does it feel more like a natural reaction to missing your wife being around?

I guess I haven't really thought about it in terms of brain chemistry. I mean... I don't really know how to tell the difference, to be honest. 

It definitely started when she wasn't around as much, but right now... it just feels like a heavy mood that won't go away. I couldn't really say if it's an internal thing or just a natural reaction, honestly. I just know I feel pretty down.

Before your wife started her full-time job three weeks ago, had you been noticing any of these feelings — the heaviness, the flatness, the loss of appetite — building up gradually, or did they truly start only after her schedule changed?

Well, when I really think about it... looking back, it didn't just start three weeks ago. I've actually had this sort of depressed, slowed-down feeling hanging around, off and on, for about three months now. It's just that these past few weeks, since she started the job, it's been the most noticeable. But yeah, it was definitely there before her schedule changed.

When you say you've had this depressed, slowed-down feeling for about three months, off and on — has there been a time during those three months when you felt noticeably better, or has it been pretty consistently there the whole time?
Well, it's been pretty consistent, I think. I mean, I haven't really had any periods where I felt noticeably better or like myself again. It's just been this steady, low feeling the whole time.

Over these past three months, besides the low mood and changes in your appetite, have you noticed any other changes — like trouble sleeping or sleeping too much, feeling unusually tired or lacking energy, difficulty concentrating, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?

Well, the sleep thing has been an issue. I mean, I'm sleeping, but it's not good sleep. It's really broken up. I keep waking up early, usually around four or five in the morning, and my mind just starts going. I start worrying about things like paying the bills, or these music tracks I've been trying to finish but just can't seem to get done. 

Because of that, I'm just so tired before the day even really begins. As for the other stuff... yeah, I definitely have less energy, and I guess I haven't really been as interested in working on my music or doing much of anything else lately.
Over these past three months, have there been any periods where you felt unusually energetic, more talkative than normal, or like you needed less sleep than usual — even for just a few days?

Well, actually... yeah, there was a time before this low period started. It was maybe a few months back. I had a few days where I didn't really need much sleep at all. 

I'd sleep for maybe three, four hours a night, tops. But the weird thing was, I didn't feel tired. I'd wake up feeling totally charged and ready to go. It honestly felt like sleeping was just... getting in the way, you know? Like I just wanted to stay up and finish the next music track I was working on, or organize these spreadsheets I had going. I just had a lot of energy for a few days there.

During those few days a few months ago when you were sleeping only 3-4 hours but felt fully energized, did you also notice that your thoughts were racing, that you were talking more than usual, or that you were taking on a lot of projects or activities at the same time?

Yeah, I definitely was. Well, my wife was actually the one who pointed it out mostly. She told me I was talking way faster than usual. I guess I was just jumping all over the place—going from talking about music plugins to these new business plans I had, and then on to local artists. 

Looking back, I could tell I wasn't really giving her much room to answer or even get a word in. I just had all these ideas going at once and wanted to get them all out.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a current depressive episode (3 months duration with increased severity over past 3 weeks) preceded by a distinct hypomanic episode (few months prior: decreased need for sleep with high energy, racing thoughts, pressured speech, flight of ideas, increased goal-directed activity). This pattern of mood episodes—hypomanic followed by depressive—is characteristic of Bipolar II Disorder. The depressive symptoms (persistent low mood, anhedonia, appetite loss, early morning awakening, fatigue, concentration difficulty) meet criteria for a major depressive episode. The prior hypomanic period (3-4 hours sleep without fatigue, pressured speech, racing thoughts, increased talkativeness, multiple simultaneous projects) meets criteria for a hypomanic episode. The temporal sequence and distinct nature of these episodes support bipolar disorder rather than unipolar depression or adjustment disorder.
